Compiler Explorer cross-compiler probe for #4492
Generated by <repo>/.github/skills/dxc-issue-triage/data/issues/4492/ce-clang-probe.py
==============================================================================

Question: DXC scales structured-buffer matrix element indices by 4 bytes
instead of the 2-byte size of a 16-bit scalar. Does the successor front
end (Clang, where HLSL support is being rebuilt) do the same?

Compilers: dxc_trunk, hlsl_clang_trunk  (Compiler Explorer, Linux Release)
Arguments: -T cs_6_2 -E testStructuredBufferMatrixLoad2 -enable-16bit-types

Reference offsets for `a[0].xy` then `a[3].zw` of a 4x4 half matrix,
derived from the type -- not from any compiler:
  row_major     [0, 2, 28, 30]   (element is 32 bytes)
  column_major  [0, 8, 22, 30]   (element is 32 bytes)

--- TRIVIAL (control)   (inline in this script)
      dxc_trunk          exit=0 crash=False f16 offsets=[0, 0] align=[2] span=2
      hlsl_clang_trunk   exit=0 crash=False f16 offsets=[0, 0] align=[2] span=2

--- minimal-matrix.hlsl   (<repo>/.github/skills/dxc-issue-triage/data/issues/4492/minimal-matrix.hlsl)
      dxc_trunk          exit=0 crash=False f16 offsets=[0, 4, 56, 60] align=[2] span=62
      hlsl_clang_trunk   exit=0 crash=False f16 offsets=[0, 8, 22, 30] align=[2] span=32

--- minimal-matrix-colmajor.hlsl   (<repo>/.github/skills/dxc-issue-triage/data/issues/4492/minimal-matrix-colmajor.hlsl)
      dxc_trunk          exit=0 crash=False f16 offsets=[0, 16, 44, 60] align=[2] span=62
      hlsl_clang_trunk   exit=0 crash=False f16 offsets=[0, 8, 22, 30] align=[2] span=32

==============================================================================
Self-tests -- if any of these fails, nothing below it is measurement.

  [PASS] dxc_trunk: control compiles, emits an f16 access at alignment 2 (exit=0, offsets=[0, 0], align=[2])
  [PASS] hlsl_clang_trunk: control compiles, emits an f16 access at alignment 2 (exit=0, offsets=[0, 0], align=[2])

  The control has no matrix, so both compilers must handle it. It fixes
  the meaning of an empty offset list below: absence of f16 accesses
  would be a dropped -enable-16bit-types, not a compiler difference.

==============================================================================
Reading

  Clang emits the same offsets with and without `#pragma pack_matrix(row_major)`: True
  -> the pragma is not acted on, so Clang answers the column-major
     question. Compare Clang against DXC's *colmajor* row only.

  minimal-matrix.hlsl
    dxc_trunk          [0, 4, 56, 60]  does NOT match this layout; exactly 2x the correct offsets
                       highest byte touched = 62 (PAST THE END OF the 32-byte element)
    hlsl_clang_trunk   [0, 8, 22, 30]  does NOT match this layout
                       highest byte touched = 32 (inside the 32-byte element)

  minimal-matrix-colmajor.hlsl
    dxc_trunk          [0, 16, 44, 60]  does NOT match this layout; exactly 2x the correct offsets
                       highest byte touched = 62 (PAST THE END OF the 32-byte element)
    hlsl_clang_trunk   [0, 8, 22, 30]  matches the type layout
                       highest byte touched = 32 (inside the 32-byte element)

  Apples-to-apples (both column-major, same source file):
    Clang [0, 8, 22, 30]   DXC [0, 16, 44, 60]
    -> Clang is correct; DXC is exactly double. The successor front
       end does not share the defect.

Caveat: Compiler Explorer's oldest DXC is 1.6.2112, which is already
inside the range where the reporter's shader reproduces, so the link
cannot show the v1.6.2104 boundary. It corroborates today's behaviour.
